known_limitations: Archer rear diagonals require live-game directional review.
Artisan NW is slightly brighter ochre than other directions; anatomical staff handedness remains uncertain.
The four SE walking poses use a shared pixel scale and source pivot; live-game motion acceptance is still required.
Subtle source lighting/color variation persists between generated walking poses.
The three isolated SW/NE/NW idle sources replace the older sheet directions. Their costume and direction are preview inspected; live turn transitions still require inspection.

SW/NE/NW sources contain baked checker backgrounds. Border-connected fill and individually reviewed enclosed windows are documented in source provenance; matching foreground colors are not globally masked.
Packed earth is one repeated tile; seam statistics and a repeated preview are supplied, and the live terrain pattern still needs inspection.

Large static props were freshly reconstructed from original sources after the original coarser sprites failed the hero-relative pixel-pitch comparison. Original props.json/gate.json and their provenance remain as superseded imports.

Source images do not form exact nearest-neighbor grids (Pixel Respecter detect_nn_scale returns 1); chosen manual grids sample visible source clusters. No resizing occurs after reconstruction. Huts retain source shading texture.
V3 reduces head width to10-11native pixels while preserving commoncell7,80x96canvas and source origins. All six poses now use v3 with documented connected checker removal.
Darker contours, redder and busier material shading, and abrupt raised-hand entry remain known roughness versus idle. Production timing and idle transitions remain subject to live review.
Updated hand pixels require equipment socket remeasurement; prior v1/v2 socket measurements are not assumed exact.
One static contact spark fades in the renderer; this is not an authored multi-frame burst.
The contact origin is measured on the reconstructed sprite, not inferred from its transparent canvas center.
SW uses one measured450px row-origin stride; source crop boundary510 avoids neighboring feet. All poses retain sharedscale and original offsets within each row.
Border-connected background removal only; any enclosed pockets remain review defects and must be inspected before promotion.
Root and pipeline inspected alternating thigh/support progression; production movement, body bob and equipment sockets remain review gates. Candidate PNGs are preserved separately.
Fixed shared sheet-row roots now correct vertical packing; no per-frame fitting or scale change. Residual sole travel0..2 native pixels remains.
Walk body65..69px versus idle63px, redder tunic and wider stance remain; this registration correction does not repair identity or body-scale drift.
Border-connected background removal only; enclosed pockets remain a visual review concern.

Baseline production frame019 used hero_walk6_nw with a 6px foot gap; corrected pixels have a 1px gap. Root viewed the corrected production frame019 and the shifted NW equipment probe passed. Residual 0..2px sole travel remains.
One measured460px source row-origin stride preserves common head/torso level; equal physical scale uses sourcecell5. Original pose offsets remain within each row.
Candidate phase/pivot and enclosed-background artifacts require review before promotion.

Revised2-to3 transition opens into wide stride, then closes through6/7; inspected for production trial. Adjacent0/1 and4/5 remain close in the generated output; equipped movement and body bob remain live review gates.

Root inspected native,4x sequence and idle comparison: upper-left/back facing and physical-left strike remain consistent through distinct extension,contact and recoil. Production timing/equipped motion acceptance remains pending.
Torso is broader and redder than accepted idle; visible crown-to-sole height is57–59px versus idle63px. These remain identity/transition caveats for production trial.

Source RGB painted pattern was removed with the recorded border-connected cleanup. Source-owner native/3x review found no visible trapped pattern pockets; the light contact-frame pixel was confirmed as a bronze highlight.
Source grid packing varies; measured planted-boot registration removes translations using one shared reconstruction pitch and a common support-sole target. No pose is independently resized.

Root inspected the final native and4x idle-to-strike0..5-to-idle comparison. Physical-left strike,contact and retraction remain consistent; common native scale and pivot are retained. Production timing/equipped motion remains a review gate.

Remaining visual differences: heads are14–15px wide versus idle12; standing body is67–68px versus idle65; dark outline and tunic colors shift. This is production-trial acceptance, not final visual polish.
Explicit source roots compensate sheet packing translations; no pose is independently fitted or resized.
Mixed-source integer grid pitches differ by about2percent from the measured1254/512 canvas ratio. That residual scale approximation is preserved in provenance.
All sources use recorded connected checker cleanup, including the individually inspected enclosed window. Final source and runtime candidates remain preserved.
Root reviewed native, 3x3 repeated, initial integrated and live game captures; accepted for production trial. Opposite edges are not exact matches and broad repeated patterns remain perceptible.
Source is unchanged. Runtime uses identical actual Pixel Respecter auto-grid reconstruction and64x64 terrain normalization as the reviewed candidate.
Root integrated world placement, roads, shade and shared registration. This manifest imports only the quiet earth tile; broad repeat structure remains a visual limitation.

Source/native/4x and independent weapon review passed for axe-v3. Root viewed all eight native poses and selected SCRIPTED production frames; the scenario verified all eight production phases and settle. Native enemy AI remains stationary, so pursuit or autonomous gameplay is not accepted.
Frames preserve the reviewed axe-v3 pixels, including the small original frame7 head offset and close adjacent0/1 and4/5 phases. Minor blade contour/angle variation from idle remains.
Generated source has an opaque checker pattern. Actual Pixel Respecter cleanup includes only recorded border fill and visually inspected hair-loop and axe/knee gaps.
One common source origin197,480, column stride406,row stride435 and cell6; no per-frame fitting or centering.
Axe is embedded in the anatomical-right/screen-left hand in all8 SW frames. Use ordinary whole monster rendering, without hero weapon overlay.

Root viewed fixed-origin native/3x palette comparison, native equipped NE grids and actual equipped NE hit. Production contact is reviewed for provisional integration; this is not final visual polish.

Each selected input is an immutable native 80x96 reconstruction. Actual Pixel Respecter cell1 reconstruction and palette snap preserve every alpha value, pixel position and common pivot[40,96]; no individual pose fitting or rescaling.

CIELAB nearest-color matching pins RGB to the accepted NE idle palette. Followthrough remains wider, the return to recovery is fast, and anatomical/material differences remain despite successful production contact integration.
Ready uses the actual accepted runtime hero_ne.png and remains pixel-identical; the obsolete candidate idle is excluded.

The selected windup, commit and recovery native inputs retain their earlier batch palette. The original batch report is historical provenance; exact active reproduction starts from these preserved native PNGs and does not rerun superseded candidate poses.
Bow/staff checks verify attachment and sampling only; they do not establish a bow draw/release or staff casting animation.

Root viewed native SW action, corrected warning poses and actual elite SW sweep contact: warning0/1/2 precedes life loss, first confirmed hit3 applies damage8 and impact, followed by followthrough4/recovery5/idle. This is provisional production integration, not final visual polish.
Selected original v1 poses0,2,3,4,5 plus corrected v2 anticipation1. Color repair restored charcoal cloth; original olive-tinted phase1 remains preserved and rejected.
One shared cell6 reconstruction with source origin280,480, column500,row490,canvas80x96,pivot40,96; no per-pose fitting or centering.

Anticipation is an outward preparatory lift. Contact3 is synchronized to the confirmed production hit; low follow-through4 and recovery retain abrupt pose and silhouette changes that still need visual refinement.
Source opaque checker removed through actual Pixel Respecter. Exact neutral-only local windows preserve pale colored skin; earlier broader color cleanup is preserved as rejected evidence.
Axe is baked into the same anatomical-right/screen-left hand in all6 SW frames. Ordinary whole monster rendering; no separate hero equipment overlay.

Only Raider SW has this six-phase action. Other raider action directions are not supplied or inferred from these frames; the former scripted SW locomotion review remains separate from this real elite combat event proof.

Common source-cell origin384,384 and pitch12 preserve phase offsets without individual fitting.
One static directional curved slash trail, not an authored animation or omnidirectional sweep area. Renderer timing/orientation remains separate.
Source genuine alpha contains partial edge pixels and faint low-alpha remnants; actual Pixel Respecter crisp reconstruction yields the reviewed binary native mask without a matte-color deletion.
The seven detached native components total only15 pixels; main curve has243 pixels. Native contact flare is broader than the requested1-3px edge, but the arc stays compact.

Native1x/3x, measured pivots and production feedback are root-reviewed for provisional integration. The two opposed-copy Sweep composition is renderer behavior, not additional authored sprite directions.
Generated source is RGB with painted checker; actual alpha request failed.
One shared cell8 scale; measured layout origins [400,608] with column704 and row416. Low poses retain source offsets rather than being independently fitted.

Root reviewed the six native phases at1x/3x, idle transitions and source-alpha comparison; production walk-phase crops and full-frame pursuit feedback are root-reviewed for provisional integration. No smooth-video claim is made.
Walking stance is narrower than idle and the carried axe has a smaller, nearly edge-on blade. Six authored phases include a close phase5-to0 transition.
Original v1 supplies phases0,1,4,5 and focused v2 supplies phases2,3. A single cell7 reconstruction and one32-color palette preserve all phase scale and color; no independent frame fitting.

Axe remains embedded in the anatomical-right/screen-right hand; no hero weapon overlay.

Root reviewed the final frozen native1x and identity3x strips after all12 source-reviewed matte windows and the common two-pixel downshift; production walk-phase crops and full-frame pursuit feedback are root-reviewed for provisional integration. No smooth-video claim is made.
The carried axe is smaller/narrower than the accepted idle blade. Crown height and silhouette differ during the walk; no claim of fully matched anatomy or polished gait.
Eight row-major source poses retain one cell6 scale, source origin190,468 and strides406,475. All frames80x96/pivot40,96; no individual fitting or rescaling.

The generated source has an opaque backdrop. Actual importer border cleanup and12 recorded source-reviewed interior windows remove background, followed by palette snapping to the accepted32-color raider_nw PNG.
Axe remains embedded in anatomical-right/screen-right hand. External ordered motion imagery is an authoring reference only and is not copied into game source assets or runtime.

Root reviewed all four actual SE pursuit frames in native 1x production crops, the native 1x/3x idle transitions and the normal 3440 live launch/House and Scion/road entry/F3 flow. Exact pixels are provisionally accepted for game integration with the documented silhouette, mask and small-axe caveats.
The walk has a narrower silhouette, mask/head variation and a smaller embedded axe than the accepted idle. These identity differences remain explicit provisional-integration caveats.

The separately generated source images use measured Pixel Respecter pitches12,12,11,12. A reviewed native_scale_group retains the contact2 reconstruction exactly; all canvases80x96/pivot40,96, visible heights55/56/54/55, and no post-reconstruction resizing.
The axe remains embedded in the anatomical-right hand. Four contact/support phases do not establish smooth playback or a complete manual combat session.

Root reviewed seven actual Wight SW production phases plus contact and the new scene; phase4 was separately covered by raster-world. Native 1x/3x idle transitions and normal 3440 live entry/F3 were also reviewed. Exact cleaned v1 pixels are provisionally accepted for game integration with narrower-torso and obscured-hip caveats.

The walk has a narrower torso than idle, and the robe obscures hip continuity. Anatomical support continuity remains difficult to establish; screen-space leading-foot position alone does not establish a repeated physical leg.
All eight phases come from the original v1 source. No v3 pose is spliced into the cycle. One cell6 reconstruction, 80x96 canvas and [40,96] pivot preserve shared placement without per-frame resizing.

Blue-biased border-distance cleanup preserves the pale phase1 hand erased by the rejected gray-distance recipe. The accepted recipe removes 20 reviewed neutral background components through 538 exact row-run windows; source RGB pixels remain unchanged.

Only SW has an authored Wight walk cycle. Root reports supported native suites/all 72 scenarios, browser 32/32, importer 10/10 and equipment checks passing. No completed manual combat or smooth-video claim is made.

Original generated stone was reconstructed by the actual Pixel Respecter; published edge_match_blend then normalized two opposite border pixels against the exact accepted palette. This import preserves that derived native source.

Root viewed native repeated and actor comparisons. The narrow repair closes opposite-edge RGB mismatches; repeating slab arrangements and interrupted joints remain. A zero edge score is not seamless visual acceptance.
The imagegen offset repair and wider eight-pixel blend were rejected. Normal-game floor shading, wall composition and visual acceptance are recorded separately.

Root reviewed native module, literal3x3wall and offline actor-context comparisons. Recurring cap motifs and mismatched masonry at module joins remain; this is not a seamless-wall claim.
